title: Lower Manhattan and the Brooklyn waterfront, compiled from NYC public records

grid.projection: local equirectangular: x = (lon − -74.26)·84515.477, y = (lat − 40.49)·111048.086 (metres); geometry stored as EPSG:4326 rounded to 1e-7°

local.description: Full geometry and every compiled attribute, for the study extent and a buffer.

context.description: Simplified geometry and reduced attributes, for surroundings.

sources.title: Terrarium elevation tiles (AWS Terrain Tiles / Mapzen)
sources.provider: Mapzen / Linux Foundation Terrain Tiles on AWS (blend of USGS 3DEP and other sources)
sources.license: Terrain Tiles attribution (https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md); USGS 3DEP is public domain
sources.crs: EPSG:3857 tiles, sampled at substrate grid cell centres
sources.method: Bilinear sample (the app's sampleTerrarium) at the centre of every 16 m cell of the substrate grid over the coverage, row-major from the north row, stored as integer centimetres. Grid west/south 19967.998 / 23040.001 m.
caveats: Terrarium blends sources and includes bathymetry; along NYC shorelines it contains artefacts down to −14 km (routing/R3).
Nominal z15 pixel is about 3.6 m at this latitude; the underlying source resolution varies by place.
Vertical datum is not stated per tile by the provider.

sources.title: Borough Boundaries
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Shoreline-clipped borough polygons. Before freezing, every ring was clipped (Sutherland–Hodgman, in the substrate grid) to the coverage plus a 64 m margin and rounded to 1e-7°; rings are stored without polygon nesting because land is filled by even-odd parity. Full boundary content hash: sha256:42ea0b7db4c561416f7322eaeac3e3418caa5e9d62a28535619a62a87ab9e054.
caveats: The shoreline is a digitised boundary at an unspecified tide; piers may or may not be included as land.
Land outside the five boroughs (New Jersey) is not in this dataset and appears as no-data, not water.

sources.title: BUILDING
sources.provider: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Every footprint whose geometry intersects the coverage box (Socrata intersects), selected fields only, as returned.
caveats: Footprints are photogrammetric or manually digitised planimetric survey; individual footprints may be outdated.
height_roof and ground_elevation are in feet and are absent or zero for some records.

sources.title: Primary Land Use Tax Lot Output (PLUTO)
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Tax-lot attributes for the 2458 distinct BBLs referenced by frozen footprints (mappluto_bbl, else base_bbl).
caveats: PLUTO describes tax lots, not buildings: land use is the lot's, and numfloors is the tallest building on the lot.
Administrative records compiled from several city agencies; not a field survey.

sources.title: Parks Properties
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Parks properties intersecting the coverage box, selected fields only, as returned.
caveats: A property boundary, not a vegetation map: plazas, playgrounds and esplanades inside parks are often paved.

sources.title: NYC Planimetric Database: Hydrography
sources.provider: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (planimetrics)
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Hydrography polygons (feature codes 2600–2660: lake, pond, river, stream, wetland, beach, bay) intersecting the coverage box. Capture rules: https://github.com/CityOfNewYork/nyc-planimetrics/blob/master/Capture_Rules.md
caveats: Not the 'Hydrography Structures' layer (6hbv-tek4), which holds piers and jetties, not water.
Open harbour and river water is mostly absent from this layer; the substrate derives open water from the shoreline instead.

sources.title: Centerline
sources.provider: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (CSCL)
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Every CSCL segment whose geometry intersects the coverage box, selected fields only, as returned. Field meanings: https://github.com/CityOfNewYork/nyc-geo-metadata/blob/main/Metadata/Metadata_StreetCenterline.md
caveats: streetwidth is the paved width in feet and is absent for many segments.
trafdir is relative to the segment's address range; nonped is not documented in the published dictionary.
Vertical level codes describe grade separation (13 = at grade), not elevation.

sources.title: 2015 Street Tree Census - Tree Data
sources.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use (https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page)
sources.method: Every 2015 census record (alive, dead or stump) in the coverage box.
caveats: Street trees only; trees in parks and private lots are not censused.
Points, not canopy; the census is from 2015.
tree_dbh is diameter at breast height in inches.

sources.title: USGS National Land Cover Database 2021: land cover and percent developed imperviousness (CONUS)
sources.provider: U.S. Geological Survey / Multi-Resolution Land Characteristics Consortium
sources.crs: EPSG:4326 (server-side nearest-neighbour reprojection of 30 m Albers cells)
sources.method: Raw class codes and impervious percent per cell over the coverage box, as returned.
caveats: NLCD is a remote-sensing product with its own error; agreement with it is not agreement with ground truth.
30 m cells; epoch 2021. Buildings and pavement are not separable.

config.label: nyc-lower-manhattan-2026-10
config.title: Lower Manhattan and the Brooklyn waterfront, compiled from NYC public records

buildings.title: Building footprints

attributes.name: footprint
attributes.transform: rounded to 1e-7°, rings closed and oriented; self-intersections flagged, not repaired

attributes.name: footprintAreaM2
attributes.transform: planar shoelace area in the substrate grid (≤0.33% scale error), outer minus holes

attributes.name: roofPlanAreaM2
attributes.transform: plan-view roof area taken as the footprint area; overhangs, setbacks and roof pitch ignored

attributes.name: roofHeightM
attributes.transform: feet × 0.3048; null where the source records 0 or nothing (dictionary: not available)

attributes.name: groundElevationM
attributes.transform: feet × 0.3048; null where absent

attributes.name: constructionYear
attributes.transform: integer; null where absent or 0

attributes.name: featureType
attributes.transform: code mapped to the data dictionary label

attributes.name: lot.landUse
attributes.transform: joined by BBL (mappluto_bbl, else base_bbl); the tax lot's land use, not the building's

attributes.name: lot.lotNumFloors
attributes.transform: floors of the tallest building on the lot; null where 0 or absent

transformations: parse Socrata strings to numbers; feet to metres
identify by DOITT feature id (BIN where no DOITT id; dummy BINs are not identifiers)
round coordinates to 1e-7°, drop repeated vertices, close and orient rings
flag self-intersections without repairing them
join PLUTO tax-lot attributes by BBL
assign each footprint to the local tile containing its area-weighted centroid; reference it from every other tile its bounds touch
context level: outer rings Douglas–Peucker simplified at 2 m; height and area kept

representation.context: simplified outer rings, height and area

caveats: Footprints meet ASPRS Class 1 (±2 ft) where photogrammetric; manually digitised ones are less accurate.
Roof plan area is the footprint area; roof height is above ground, not above sea level.
PLUTO land use and floors describe the tax lot, not the individual building.

streets.title: Street centrelines and modelled surfaces

attributes.name: geometry
attributes.transform: contiguous MultiLineString parts joined, rounded to 1e-7°, consecutive duplicates removed

attributes.name: lengthM
attributes.transform: planar length in the substrate grid (SHAPE__Length is marked 'do not use' by the provider)

attributes.name: roadClass
attributes.transform: code mapped to the data dictionary label

attributes.name: widthM
attributes.transform: paved width in feet × 0.3048; null where 0 or absent

attributes.name: trafficDirection
attributes.transform: FT/TF/TW/NV mapped; relative to the address range, which the street graph assumes runs from the first to the last vertex (CSCL convention, not verified per segment)

attributes.name: travelLanes
attributes.transform: integer; null where absent

attributes.name: levelCodes
attributes.transform: raw codes; 13 = at grade, others grade-separated

attributes.name: pedestrianExcluded
attributes.transform: true for non-physical segments, highways, ramps, tunnels, and any non-empty nonped (undocumented; treated conservatively)

attributes.name: surface
attributes.transform: centreline offset by half the recorded width; null where the width is unknown; not the planimetric roadbed

attributes.name: surfaceAreaM2
attributes.transform: planar area of the modelled surface

transformations: join contiguous MultiLineString parts; round coordinates to 1e-7°
map CSCL codes (rw_type, trafdir, status) to labels; feet to metres
mark segments not on the ground (paper streets, non-physical segments, ferry routes)
offset centrelines by half the recorded width to model a street surface where the width is known
assign each segment to the tile containing its length midpoint; reference it from every other tile it crosses
context level: Douglas–Peucker at 4 m; class and width kept; physical segments only

representation.local: full centrelines, attributes and modelled surfaces
representation.context: simplified physical centrelines with class and width

caveats: Modelled surfaces ignore medians, curb returns and junction geometry; they are not the planimetric roadbed.
Widths are unknown for a large share of segments and are never filled.

streetGraph.title: Street graph
streetGraph.geometry: nodes (intersections, endpoints, continuations) and edges (physical street segments)

attributes.name: nodes
attributes.transform: segment endpoints merged within 0.5 m on the same CSCL level

attributes.name: elevationM
attributes.transform: bilinear sample of the elevation lattice at at-grade nodes; null near artefacts or not at grade

attributes.name: slope
attributes.transform: (to − from elevation) / length for at-grade edges

transformations: endpoint keys from rounded positions and level codes
union-find merge within tolerance
degree and kind from compiled edges
boundary flag where the coverage truncates topology
node owned by its tile (boundary nodes outside coverage by their first edge's tile); edge owned with its segment

representation.local: nodes and edges with external-node references

caveats: Topology only: no turn restrictions, signals or lane connectivity.
Traffic direction assumes the address range runs from the first to the last vertex.

pedestrianGraph.title: Pedestrian access (centreline level)

attributes.name: excluded
attributes.transform: excluded with a reason: not physical, highway/ramp/tunnel, or a non-empty nonped flag

transformations: classify each street-graph edge as usable by pedestrians or excluded, with the reason
caveats: Not sidewalk geometry: both sides of a street are one edge.
nonped is undocumented in the published dictionary and is treated conservatively.

surfaceFlowGraph.title: Surface-flow structure (experimental)
surfaceFlowGraph.geometry: street nodes, terrain low points and open-water receivers with oriented links

attributes.name: edges
attributes.transform: street edges oriented downhill (flat below 0.002); sinks within 40 m of open water linked to it; terrain low points linked to the nearest street node within 24 m

transformations: orient at-grade street edges by sampled elevation
identify street-network sinks
link sinks to open-water receivers
detect strict terrain low points on land above 0 m
link low points to nearby street nodes
caveats: Experimental structure for a future comparison with D8; not used by any routed result.
Not a sewer or drainage-network model: no pipes, inlets, capacities, volumes or timing.
Street grades come from sampled ground elevation at nodes; grade-separated edges are excluded.

elevation.title: Ground elevation

attributes.name: valuesCm
attributes.transform: bilinear sample at local-cell centres, integer centimetres; context cells are the mean of 4 × 4 local cells, null if any is missing

transformations: sample Terrarium at local cell centres (at fetch)
store integer centimetres
aggregate whole local cells for context
caveats: Terrarium blends sources and includes bathymetry; shoreline artefacts far below sea level are kept and counted, not repaired.
The app's storm routing still loads elevation itself; this layer is the substrate's own record and is not substituted into routed experiments.
No synthetic or illustrative elevation is ever written into the substrate.

landCover.title: Reference land cover (NLCD 2021)
landCover.geometry: per-tile class counts and reference shares

attributes.name: classCounts
attributes.transform: count of 30 m cells whose centre falls in the tile and the coverage

attributes.name: reference
attributes.transform: water = class 11 share; impervious = mean percent imperviousness of non-water cells over all cells; pervious = remainder

transformations: assign 30 m cells to tiles by centre
count classes; compute water, impervious and pervious shares
caveats: A reference map with its own error, kept separate from the AI classification and never written into it.
Buildings and pavement are not separable; epoch 2021.

vegetation.title: Street trees and park properties

attributes.name: trees.position
attributes.transform: rounded to 1e-7°

attributes.name: trees.dbhCm
attributes.transform: inches × 2.54; null where 0 or absent (stumps record 0)

attributes.name: trees.status
attributes.transform: as recorded in 2015 (Alive, Dead, Stump)

attributes.name: parkProperties.geometry
attributes.transform: normalised like footprints; a property boundary, not vegetation

transformations: round positions; inches to centimetres
normalise park polygons
assign trees by position and parks by centroid
caveats: Street trees only (2015 census), as points, not canopy.
Park properties include paved plazas and playgrounds; they are not a vegetation map.

water.title: Open water and inland water bodies
water.geometry: land/water mask (8 m local, 32 m context); inland water polygons

attributes.name: mask
attributes.transform: cell centres inside shoreline-clipped borough land (even-odd scanline) are L, others W; N outside the declared coverage

attributes.name: openWaterAreaM2
attributes.transform: W cells × cell area

attributes.name: bodies
attributes.transform: inland water polygons, normalised like footprints

transformations: fill shoreline-clipped borough land by even-odd scanline at cell centres
everything else inside coverage is open water
outside coverage is no-data, not water
normalise inland water polygons
caveats: Open water is receiving water: it is never counted as retention or pervious area.
The shoreline is a digitised boundary at an unspecified tide; New Jersey is not in the source and is no-data.

Context features are simplifications of compiled local features

Elevation cells far below sea level (source artefacts, kept)
